gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a wired headset that works on Xbox costs $69.99 on its maker's store today (HyperX Cloud III, down from $99.99), while the three USB desk mics priced here (Maono DGM20 $43.99, FIFINE AM8 $56.99, Maono PD200XS $89.99) leave Xbox off their maker compatibility lists and still need headphones on top.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches and got no result pages, so there was no cited rival page to compare against. Its own answer's only price line was 'Often cheaper overall' for a headset and 'Can cost more' for a mic, with no model, no dollar figure and no platform caveat. A priced, platform-checked list of the whole category is new against that.
decides: It backs the headset as the default and puts a number on it. A mic route only costs less if the shopper already owns headphones and plays on PC or PlayStation. The cheapest Xbox-ready headset here is the EKSA E900 at $34.99, and the HyperX Cloud III at $69.99 lists PC, PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, Switch, Mac and mobile. Among the mics, the FIFINE AM8 at $56.99 costs $13 less than the Cloud III but works only on PC, PS4 and PS5, and Fifine recommends speaking 2 to 6 inches from it, so in practice it needs an arm (the AM8T kit with arm is $67.99). The clip-on ModMic USB 2 at $99.95 costs more than the Cloud III headset alone. For Xbox owners keeping their headphones, the mic route is the ModMic Uni 2+ ($64.95) plus Antlion's Y adapter ($12.95), $77.90 in total. That is $7.91 more than the Cloud III.
